It has been stated that parents of the complainant/respondent spent sufficient amount at the time of marriage and gave dowry articles to the appellant and his family members as per their demands.

However, she was subjected to mental and physical torture, beatings and other cruelties Prem Prakash vs Urmila on 16 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48520552/

complainant has narrated various incidents of abuses, humiliation and beatings by the appellant and his family members.
The matter was even reported to Police also on 03.06.2008 and appellant and his brother were also sent to jail by learned SEM.

But, even after several dates of hearing before CAW Cell, appellant continued to harass, torture and give beatings to the respondent and thrown her out of matrimonial house and also,
flatly refused to take her back.
With the help of CAW officials, the respondent was again sent back to her matrimonial house on 04.08.2008.
Thereafter, the respondent was sent back to her parental house in wearing clothes only on the occasions of Rakhi and Bhai Dooj and she was not given any jewellery.
In order to save her marriage, the respondent/complainant continued to reside in the matrimonial home with the hope that the appellant would mend his behavior.

Despite facing continuous harassment,
humiliation, and ill-treatment, she chose to bear all the atrocities for the sake of preserving the marital relationship.
However, the appellant failed to change his conduct, which ultimately compelled her to take legal recourse and she filed a complaint against appellant with PS Neb Sarai on 17.04.2009.
On 20.04.2009, when the appellant and his brother came to know about that complaint, they started throwing household articles and also gave beatings to complainant/respondent.
Consequently, respondent called the police and appellant and madhu by madhu jain

Thereafter, the appellant and his brother did not return.

Having no other option,
respondent started living with his sister Kavita, who was also residing in another portion of matrimonial house being the wife of brother of appellant.
Since all the clothes and articles of the respondent were lying in locked house, she made requests to appellant and his family members to let her stay in matrimonial house which they refused.

Feeling aggrieved with the atrocities committed upon her by the appellant and his family members by refusing shelter, food, clothing and other day to day requirements, the respondent filed a petition under Section 12 of DV Act before the learned Trial court seeking various reliefs.

It has been stated that appellant had been living separately since April 2009 and he filed a petition under Section 9 of HMA for restitution of conjugal rights and got issued a legal notice which was duly served upon the respondent.
It has also been stated that the respondent is residing in the house which is in the name of mother of appellant and she has no right to force his parents to leave that house.

4. Both the parties filed their income and expenditure affidavits before the learned trial court and thereafter, led their respective evidences.

Learned Trial court after considering the evidence led by both the parties and submissions made by them, disposed of the petition under Section 12 of DV thereby, granting Rs.5,000/- per month towards maintenance i.e. Rs.3,000/- per month for respondent and Rs.2,000/- per month for the child.
Learned trial court also awarded an amount of Rs.10,000/- as compensation under Section 22 of DV Act.

Aggrieved of the same, the appellant /
husband has preferred the present appeal.

6.

The appeal is duly contested by the respondent by filing reply wherein it has been stated that the present appeal has been filed by the appellant only to harass the respondent and her minor son and to deprive them of their valuable rights to get maintenance and residence.
Hence, the same is liable to be dismissed.

7. Learned counsel for the appellant has vehemently argued that learned trial court has granted maintenance at an exorbitant CA No.357/2023 madhu Digitally signed by madhu jain Date:

It has been stated that vide order dated 20.08.2009 interim maintenance of Rs.2,000/- per month was granted by learned trial court for both respondent and minor son and since, the respondent was aware of the condition of the appellant she did not challenge the same by filing any appeal against that order.
From the same, it is apparent that respondent is earning sufficiently hence, she does not require any maintenance.

Learned counsel further argued that learned trial court erred in passing the impugned judgment as it has failed to take into account that respondent had failed to comply with the vacating order dated 29.05.2009, and instead, continued to unlawfully occupy the house owned by the appellant's mother and a separate possession suit filed by the appellant's parents in this regard is pending adjudication.
He further pointed out that the respondent and her sister are occupying another property owned by the appellant's father, forcing the appellant's family to live in rented accommodation since 2009.

It has been argued that respondent and her sister have filed multiple false and frivolous complaints against the appellant and his family members including FIRs No.45/2010 and 46/2010 under Sections 406/498A/34 IPC.

It has been argued that the minor child of the parties is receiving education under the EWS scheme free of cost and now he has madhu by madhu jain Date:

Learned counsel also argued that respondent is living a comfortable life and is earning sufficiently which is evident from the fact that she is filing multiple litigation against the appellant and his family members and spending huge amount on legal proceedings whereas, the appellant is residing in rental accommodation and suffering from various health problems.

It has been argued that the impugned judgment passed by the learned trial court is erroneous and based on a misapprehension of the appellant's financial position and without considering the fact that there is no supporting evidence to the averments Prem Prakash vs Urmila on 16 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48520552/
4 made by the respondent with respect to incidents of domestic violence.
Moreover, the appellant has been regularly complying with the maintenance orders passed by the court.

Hence, it is submitted that the respondent is not entitled to the relief granted,
and the impugned judgment deserves to be set aside.
Besides addressing oral arguments, written arguments have also been filed on behalf of the appellant.

8. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent argued that learned trial court has rightly passed the impugned judgment giving detailed observations and after considering the entire material placed on record as well as the evidence led by both the parties and thus, there is no reason to interfere in the findings of the learned trial court.

Further, learned trial madhu by madhu jain CA No.357/2023 jain Date:
2025.04.17 15:47:36 Prem Prakash Vs. Urmila +0530 court has also duly considered the facts of the case and has very fairly assessed the income of the appellant on minimum wage rate and rightly awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/- per month for the respondent and minor child.

Learned counsel has argued that all the contentions raised before this court by the appellant have already been dealt in detail by the learned trial court and thus, there is no illegality or impropriety in the impugned judgment.
Therefore, the appeal is liable to be dismissed.
9. I have heard learned counsels for both the sides and have perused the record and relevant provisions of law.
10. The matrimonial alliance between the parties is admitted.
It is also an admitted fact that from the wedlock of the parties, one son was born, who is in the care and custody of the respondent.
During the course of arguments, respondent has stated that child has just completed 12th class.
It has also come on record that the parties are living separately since April 2009.
11. The grievances of the appellant are that the order granting Rs.5,000/- monthly maintenance from the date of the complaint is excessive in view of the financial condition of the appellant.

Further, earlier an interim maintenance of Rs.2,000/- was accepted by the respondent without challenge, which shows that the respondent was aware of the appellant's CA No.357/2023 madhu by Date:
jain 2025.04.17 15:47:40 +0530 limited means.

Also, the respondent is living in the house belonging to the appellant's mother and has failed to comply with a court order to vacate the same and instead continues to occupy the same causing the appellant and his family to live in a rented accommodation.
It has been contended that the appellant is suffering from health issues and is already complying with maintenance orders and thus, the respondent is not liable to any maintenance.

12. Before proceeding further, it would be relevant to mention here that the purpose of domestic violence laws, particularly the DV Act, is to safeguard the rights of individuals, especially women,
who are subjected to abuse within the confines of their homes.

These laws recognize that domestic Prem Prakash vs Urmila on 16 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48520552/
5 violence is not limited to physical harm but also includes emotional, verbal, sexual, and economic abuse.

The primary aim is to ensure the safety, dignity, and well-being of victims by providing them with immediate relief and long-term protection through legal remedies such as protection orders,
residence rights, maintenance, and compensation.

13. Perusal of the impugned judgment shows that in the present case, while disposing of the petition filed by the respondent, learned trial court has not granted any relief under Section 18 and 19 of DV Act.

With respect to the relief under Section 20 and 22 DV Act, before concluding the findings regarding CA No.357/2023 madhu by Date:
jain 2025.04.17 15:47:45 +0530 income of the appellant, learned trial court has dealt in detail the income & expenditure filed by the appellant as well as evidence led in this regard.
14.

It may be mentioned that the law is well settled that the test for determination of maintenance /
monetary relief contemplated under the Act depends upon the financial status of the parties and the standard of living of the husband to which the wife was accustomed to in her matrimonial home.
The monetary reliefs should neither be too extravagant which may become oppressive and unbearable for the respondent nor it should be so meager so as to drive the wife to destitution and hardship.
A careful and just balance has to be drawn between the relevant factors pertaining to financial position and status of both the parties.

15. Further, it will not be out of place to mention here that in matrimonial matters, on the issue of maintenance/other monetary reliefs honest disclosure of facts and figures by parties is rarely seen.
The husband, wherever possible, tends to conceal his income and assets whereas wife tends to put forth unrealistic and excessive claim for such reliefs.
Present case is also no exception to this rule.

16. A bare perusal of impugned judgment shows that learned trial court has categorically mentioned that in the income and expenditure affidavit, appellant has given his educational CA No.357/2023 madhu by Date:
Prem Prakash Vs. Urmila jain 2025.04.17 qualification as 9th Pass and is self employed as a mechanic.

Though he has mentioned his income as NIL but being an unskilled labour, his income has been assessed as Rs.17,494/- as per the order dated 23.10.2023 of Office of Commissioner (Labour) Government of NCT of Delhi.

sentences.text: In the income & expenditure affidavit, appellant had mentioned his monthly income as of Rs.5,000/- per month and has shown his expenses as Rs.2,000/- towards rent, Rs.2,000/- towards groceries and Rs.500/- towards water and electricity.
He has also stated that he is having a vehicle make Bajaj CT 100 and mobile phone.
He has further stated that he is also paying maintenance of Rs.2,000/- per month to the respondent awarded towards interim maintenance.
From the same, it can be presumed that the appellant has not disclosed his true income which is within his special knowledge.
Also, the appellant has failed to provide any plausible explanation as to how he is managing his expenses despite declaring very low or no income.

This raises doubts about the authenticity of his financial disclosures and supports the inference that he is concealing his true income to avoid paying a fair amount of maintenance to the Prem Prakash vs Urmila on 16 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48520552/
6 respondent.

17. Despite the appellant's vague and questionable claims, learned trial court did not rely solely on his affidavit but instead took a fair and objective approach and assessed his CA No.357/2023 madhu by Prem Prakash Vs. Urmila jain Date:
2025.04.17 income by referring to an official government order that specifies the minimum wages for unskilled laborers in Delhi i.e. Rs.17,494/- per month.
This clearly suggests that learned trial court has adopted a just and balanced approached in assessing the earning capacity of the appellant.
Moreso, the findings of learned trial court are duly corroborated by the cross examination of appellant wherein he has not given plausible explanation with respect to having PAN Card.

Hence, this court finds no illegality or error in the trial court's conclusion of assessing the income and awarding Rs.5,000/- per month i.e. Rs.3,000/- for the respondent and Rs.2,000/- for the child, as it was based on a well established legal principle.

18. Now coming to the contention raised on behalf of the appellant that respondent is living in the house belonging to the appellant's mother and has failed to comply with a court order to vacate the same and instead continues to occupy the same causing the appellant and his family to live in a rented accommodation.

Admittedly, a suit of possession has been filed by the parents of the appellant with the respect to the property where respondent is residing and the same is pending adjudication before the Hon'ble High Court.

Moreover, no relief under Section 19 of DV Act has been awarded in favour of the respondent by the learned trial court madhu by madhu jain CA No.357/2023 jain Date:
2025.04.17 15:47:58 +0530 and thus, this argument of the appellant does not bear any force as the same is subject to the outcome of the appeal pending before Hon'ble High Court.
19. Another contention raised by the appellant is regarding his health issues, which he claims to have impacted his earning capacity.
However, upon careful examination of the record, it is evident that the appellant has only submitted photocopies of certain medical prescriptions.
These documents, in themselves, do not establish that the appellant is suffering from any specific illness or medical condition that would prevent him from working or earning a livelihood.
Additionally, the appellant has also placed on record certain blood test reports.
These report does not conclusively indicate any serious health condition of the appellant.

In the absence of a proper medical diagnosis or certification from a recognized medical professional clearly stating that the appellant is unfit for work due to health reasons, this contention of the appellant remains unsupported and unsubstantiated.

Therefore, this court finds that there is no credible or sufficient medical evidence on record to support the appellant's assertion that his health issues prevent him from fulfilling his financial responsibilities.

Even learned trial court has also correctly observed that no reliance can be placed on the said medical documents as none of these madhu Digitally signed CA No.357/2023 jain by madhu jain Date: 2025.04.17 15:48:02 +0530 prescriptions advice that he should not work or that he is on bed rest.
Thus, this contention also does not hold any merit.

sentences.text: In the present case, it is an undisputed fact that the minor son of the parties is under the care and custody of the respondent (mother) and is currently pursuing his education, having just completed his 12th class.
This clearly establishes that the respondent continues to bear the primary responsibility for the child's upbringing and educational needs.

It is settled principle of law that a father is legally and morally bound to support his child and a husband is duty bound to maintain his legally wedded wife, especially when she is unable to sustain herself independently.

Thus, learned trial court has not erred in awarding a sum of Rs.5,000/- per month i.e. Rs.3,000/- and Rs.2,000/-
for respondent and minor son, respectively and the same has been awarded considering the prevailing cost of living and the financial needs of the parties.
Furthermore, the trial court has also awarded a compensation of Rs.10,000/- to the respondent.

This amount is neither excessive nor punitive; rather, it is a fair and just sum, taking into account the circumstances of the case, including the history of litigation, the emotional and financial stress endured by the respondent and the conduct of the appellant.
The conclusion of the learned trial court has been arrived at after due application of mind, based on relevant legal principles and the factual madhu by madhu jain

Date:
jain 2025.04.17 15:48:06 +0530 matrix of the case.

The relief so granted is just, fair,
and in accordance with the law.
21. In view of the above findings, I find no illegality and impropriety in the impugned judgment dated 02.12.2023 passed by the learned trial court.
As such, the impugned order is upheld and the appeal is accordingly, dismissed.
22. Trial Court Record be sent back along with copy of this judgment.
